reductionPolicy: Coverage may be reduced only by an explicit, reviewed scope decision with rationale, owner, affected requirements, and compensating tests.
boundary: These are synthetic software coverage contracts, not physical devices, emulators, drivers, hardware validation, HIL, regulator approval, accreditation, or certification.

families.requested: USB, PCIe, Thunderbolt, and other transport devices
families.contract: enumeration, descriptors/configuration, queues/endpoints, reset, hot-plug, power, DMA, and error recovery

families.requested: Keyboards, mice, touchscreens, and HID sensors
families.contract: reports, usages, contact/button state, debounce, malformed reports, disconnect, and rate limits
stream formats, buffers, timestamps, underrun/overrun, format negotiation, and synchronization
command queues, buffers, modes, fences, reset, memory bounds, and display timing
frames, formats, metadata, exposure controls, buffers, timestamps, and dropped-frame recovery

families.requested: Serial, UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, and GPIO devices
families.contract: framing, addressing, direction, arbitration, pin state, timeouts, and bus faults
sample ranges, calibration, units, conversion timing, saturation, and channel faults
telemetry, charging states, limits, thermal faults, safe shutdown, and persistence boundaries

families.requested: Secure elements, TPMs, and cryptographic accelerators
families.contract: command authorization, key handles, monotonic counters, zeroization, malformed input, and error containment
discovery, association, control/data channels, radio state, credentials boundary, and link recovery

families.requested: Storage controllers, RAID, NVMe, and filesystems
families.contract: queues, namespaces, metadata, flush/order, redundancy state, media errors, and recovery
feature negotiation, shared rings, notification, migration/reset, isolation, and malformed descriptors
identity records, authentication attempts, privacy boundary, lockout, cancellation, and replay resistance
observability, alarm/fault states, watchdog, safe-state transition, audit trail, and no autonomous safety claim
function discovery, dependency ordering, partial failure, insertion/removal, resource ownership, and rollback
